properties.SITE_FEATURE_DESCRIPTION: This OU was deleted from the NPL on November 8, 2010. Cleanup activities included excavation and disposal of some contaminated material, installing a vapor barrier below buildings, and maintenance of a concrete cover that protects from exposure. Supplemental Standards, in accordance with 40 CFR Part 192, along with an unreasonably high cost of full cleanup, were used to leave some contamination in place. Because of this, there are land use rules, known as Institutional Controls (ICs), in place that keep the property safe for use. These rules include maintaining the concrete cover, annual indoor radon air monitoring reports, restrictions on drilling and using groundwater, restrictions on disturbing the subsurface and special ordinances for materials management.

These OUs were deleted from the NPL on November 8, 2010. Cleanup activities include excavation, disposal, groundwater monitoring, and implementation of ICs. Some contamination was left in place using the supplemental standards in 40 CFR part 192 and area averaged calculations. The ICs on this property are a restriction on groundwater usage, a zoning prohibition on residential development, maintenance of a concrete cover, an ordinance regarding materials management, and an informational IC about drilling groundwater wells with the Colorado State Engineer.

The soil portion of this OU was deleted from the NPL on November 8, 2010. Cleanup activities included excavation and eventual off-site disposal of contaminated soils and bioremediation of oil impacted soils.  The groundwater at OU8 is the only portion of the Denver Radium Superfund site that remains on the National Priorities List. Groundwater monitoring is ongoing. This includes an area of groundwater below the Overland Golf Course where contamination is still being monitored. EPA and the State of Colorado continue to sample the groundwater and track the contamination. All private drinking water and water features on the golf course are supplied via municipal water supply, and using the groundwater is prohibited.
